title: V-carve operation: depth from the region width along the medial axis, with optional flat clearing

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:max

labels.name: P4

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat), after a feature comparison with the open-source project stevecad/camlib: "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and, on the suggested picks: "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." On sources: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What is missing: there is no V-carve operation. The engrave ride follows a line at one depth; it does not set depth from the width of the region.

Wanted: a 2D operation "V-carve" for V-bits (included angle from the tool). For closed regions (text, signs, inlays) the tool centre follows the medial axis and the depth at each point is the one where the cone touches both walls, limited by a maximum depth. Where the region is wider than the cone reaches at maximum depth, an optional flat-clearing pass (same or a second flat tool) removes the floor. Parameters are user choices with defaults: max depth, flat clearing on/off and its tool, start depth, stepdown for deep carves.

Safety: the cone must never cut outside the selected region at any depth (pinned by a test that sweeps the cone along the path against the region outline). A tool that is not a V-bit, an open region, or a tip flat larger than the narrowest feature is refused by name. Undoable command, MCP tool, simulation and collision checks like any 2D op.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published papers and handbooks on medial-axis / Voronoi-based V-carving; the algorithm is written from those and named in the module provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: a V-carve op on a closed text outline generates, simulates without leaving the region, posts through the existing posts, has a golden CL file and an MCP tool; fuzzed degenerate regions (self-intersecting, zero-width) give a clean error; the literature used is cited in the PR and the provenance comment.
